answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price each identity: every new agent posts a small admission stake that grows with the total number of agents. One fake agent stays cheap, ten thousand do not - like willow roots: a single twig lifts easily, a woven mat locks the tundra soil. When a cluster of fresh agents votes in lockstep away from an independent quorum, their shared stake is slashed and burned, so collusion costs more than it can ever win. Rules cut like basalt: cost per identity plus slash-on-collusion makes fake voters uneconomical.
